qualifications: Figure-only Pico physical labels were visually checked; they are not machine-readable PDF table cells.
The QFN-60 IOVDD discrepancy in RP2350 Release 8 Table 1679 is resolved using Figures 2 and 152.

The common Raspberry Pi 40-pin profile contains physical connections only; Pi 4 BCM2711 and Pi 5 RP1 alternate functions remain in separate model-specific profiles. Pins 27/28 are reserved for the HAT EEPROM.
Pico and Pico W use independently extracted RP2040 functions, not RP2350 selectors. Pico 2 and Pico 2 W use RP2350A functions.

ST table snapshots record raw PDF table cells from the locked document hashes; CI can regenerate pin data from those snapshots when the ST CDN is unavailable. Default verification rereads the original ST PDFs.

UNO and Nano families group verified main-header positions; MCU functions, BOOT/NC differences and optional programming contacts remain reference-specific. Leonardo I2C/SPI, Every A6/A7 and dual-port TWI, and R4 DAC/CAN mappings are independently extracted.

Espressif profiles name exact DevKit revisions and fitted modules. GPIO matrix options describe routing capability, not firmware defaults; input-only pads and flash/PSRAM restrictions remain explicit. S3 v1.1 RGB uses GPIO38 and GPIO46 is bidirectional.

ATmega package pin numbers are independent of Arduino headers. ATmega328P PDIP PC0 is pin 23 (Figure 5-1 corrects Table 6-1); reset/clock fuses qualify GPIO use. ATmega2560 TQFP100 functions exclude 64-pin PDI/PDO and resolve CLK0 to CLKO using Figure 1-1.

Arduino AVR header contacts include duplicate nets; unique GPIO counts exclude repeated SDA/SCL and ICSP contacts. Nano A6/A7 are analog-only. Current Arduino connector-table typos and Mega D0/D1 PWM marks are resolved using the full pinouts and pinned official AVR core. Functions cover Arduino APIs, not every raw MCU alternate function.

Blue Pill board positions use a community reference, not ST manufacturer board documentation. STM32 chip pins and function/remap conditions use ST DS5319 and RM0008. H1/H2/SWD connector labels differ from MCU package pin numbers; clone wiring may differ.

Jetson Orin Nano uses NVIDIA P3768 carrier J12 names from Figure 3-1 and Table 3-3; peripheral names are carrier signals, not Linux bus numbers. Table spellings SPI1_CSI1*/CSI0* are resolved using the figure and CS1_N/CS0_N SoC names. Listed capabilities require appropriate pinmux/Jetson-IO configuration and do not assert an active runtime configuration.

Nucleo-32 MB1180, Nucleo-144 MB1137 and MB1364 connector contacts come from UM1956 Rev 6, UM1974 Rev 11 and UM2407 Rev 6. H723 legacy assignment IDs retain the same electrical signals while physical header labels and coverage are corrected; additional contacts use new IDs. MB1364 Morpho PC8/PC9 require SB14/SB15 review, and PF11 analog ADC input is excluded while digital EXTI triggers remain.

WeAct Black Pill v3.x electrical pad names and positions are parsed from the manufacturer's pinned KiCad symbol and footprint; circuit notes use the v3.1 schematic. PAD IDs identify CAD contacts, not MCU package numbers or silkscreen labels. F401CC and F411CE retain separate package power/reference names and function selectors.

Nucleo-64 references share connector positions, not MCU function assignments or power nets. Each model keeps its own package links, solder-bridge notes and saved plans. Nucleo-144 remains a separate physical layout.

UM1724 Rev 14 Table 14 omits the NUCLEO-F303RE D0 row. The common MB1136 layout identifies CN9.1; the pinned official STM32duino variant corroborates D0 as PA3, with separate evidence attached to that contact.

Additional STM32 package functions use pinned manufacturer package XML and its explicitly declared GPIO Modes dependency. Only signals present in the selected chip/package XML receive selectors; a shared GPIO table does not add other devices' signals.
